a1.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab's glossary defines "Full-time equivalent employees" as the total number of hours worked divided by a 40-hour work week for full-time, part-time, and temporary employees and persons employed on a contract basis.
items.quote: Full-time equivalent employees: Represents the total number of hours worked divided by a 40-hour work week for the following categories: full-time, part-time, and temporary employees and persons employed on a contract basis.
items.definition: Represents the total number of hours worked divided by a 40-hour work week for the following categories: full-time, part-time, and temporary employees and persons employed on a contract basis.

a1.SCHW.differs_because: The definition is for full-time equivalent employees (all employees), not Schwab's advisor headcount.
a1.SCHW.reason: No passage defines "advisor headcount"; the only firm definition is for full-time equivalent employees, a different, wider measure.

a2.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV reports approximately 30,690 employees, including full- and part-time employees and excluding clerical workers.
items.quote: Approximately how many employees do you have? Include full- and part-time employees but do not include any clerical workers. 30690

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV reports that approximately 4,127 of the employees reported in Item 5.A perform investment advisory functions (including research).
items.quote: Approximately how many of the employees reported in 5.A. perform investment advisory functions (including research)? 4127

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV reports that approximately 16,763 employees are registered representatives of a broker-dealer.
items.quote: Approximately how many of the employees reported in 5.A. are registered representatives of a broker-dealer? 16763

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV reports that approximately 6,584 employees are registered with one or more state securities authorities as investment adviser representatives.
items.quote: Approximately how many of the employees reported in 5.A. are registered with one or more state securities authorities as investment adviser representatives? 6584

a2.SCHW.differs_because: These are Form ADV Item 5 regulatory employee counts (total employees and employees in advisory/registered categories), not a Schwab "advisor headcount" metric.
a2.SCHW.reason: Schwab discloses no advisor-headcount figure; it only mentions growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors qualitatively, and the closest reported figures are Form ADV employee counts.

a3.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV states that the employee count includes full- and part-time employees.
items.quote: Include full- and part-time employees but do not include any clerical workers.

items.text: Schwab's full-time equivalent employee definition includes full-time, part-time, and temporary employees and persons employed on a contract basis.
items.quote: Represents the total number of hours worked divided by a 40-hour work week for the following categories: full-time, part-time, and temporary employees and persons employed on a contract basis.

a3.SCHW.differs_because: These inclusion statements describe all-employee measures (Form ADV total employees and full-time equivalent employees), not a Schwab advisor-headcount definition.
a3.SCHW.reason: No advisor-headcount definition exists to state inclusions; only related all-employee counting rules state what is included.

a4.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab's Form ADV states that the employee count does not include clerical workers.
items.quote: do not include any clerical workers

a4.SCHW.differs_because: This exclusion applies to the Form ADV total-employee count, not to a Schwab advisor-headcount definition.
a4.SCHW.reason: No advisor-headcount definition exists to state exclusions; the only exclusion stated is for clerical workers in the Form ADV employee count.

items.quote:

  Independent contractors                               5,065                4,961                5,019

items.text: Raymond James states that financial advisors primarily affiliate with the firm directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

a1.RJF.reason: Passages state the composition and affiliation model underlying the advisor headcount metric, so these are facts.

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Written definition: a count with no written definition at Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('Financial advisors (actual)', EDJ-10K-2025#130); publishes no count of this metric; reports a related figure instead at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('perform investment advisory functions (including research)? 4127', SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1); stated by Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Independent contractor advisors: not stated by Morgan Stanley, Merrill (Bank of America Corporation); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('Through the Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients', SCHW-10K-2025#23); stated by Edward Jones ('The Partnership’s financial advisors are employees or partners of the Partnership.', EDJ-10K-2025#35); counted by Raymond James Financial ('Independent contractors 5,065', RJF-10K-2025#227).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Business lines in the count: counted by Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada', EDJ-10K-2025#145), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation; excluded by Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Date of the registered count: dated for Morgan Stanley (2020-12-31, 'Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones (2025-12-31, 'At year end 20,425', EDJ-10K-2025#130), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) (2023-12-31, 'Total wealth advisors (3) 18,916', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial (2025-09-30, 'Total advisors 8,943', RJF-10K-2025#227); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation.

Morgan Stanley - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2020-12-31 (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (MS-SUPP-2025Q4, MS-SUPP-2026Q1, MS-SUPP-2026Q2, MS-SUPP-2026Q3).

Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2023-12-31 (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (BAC-SUPP-2025Q4, BAC-SUPP-2026Q1, BAC-SUPP-2026Q2, BAC-SUPP-2026Q3).

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says that as one of the largest U.S. investment services firms, it can spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large client base and harness resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.
items.quote: Scale and Size of the Business - As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.

items.text: Schwab says operating efficiency and shared infrastructure across businesses, coupled with scale, create a cost advantage that lets it price competitively while profitably serving clients across channels.
items.quote: Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.

items.text: Schwab's scale and efficiency initiatives keep its cost-to-serve clients low so it can reinvest in growth.
items.quote: These initiatives, which are primarily centered within service, operations, and technology, are a win for clients and are also helping enable us to keep our cost-to-serve clients low so that we can reinvest in our growth.

items.text: Schwab's scale combined with expense discipline decreased its cost per account 20% over the last five years while keeping it the industry leader on expense on client assets (EOCA).
items.quote: Our scale, combined with our expense discipline, has allowed us to decrease our cost per account 20% over the last five years while driving our ability to remain the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets, or EOCA

items.text: Schwab leverages its scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth, and 90% of accounts are opened digitally.
items.quote: Leverage our scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth 90% Accounts opened digitally

items.text: Schwab couples its scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low and keep products and solutions affordable.
items.quote: management works to couple Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low and ensure that products and solutions are affordable as well as responsive to client needs.

items.text: Schwab says leadership at its scale creates advantages that compound over time.
items.quote: Leadership at this scale creates advantages that compound over time.

items.text: Schwab says its product and capability breadth, people plus AI, and scale create a unique platform advantage difficult for competitors to match.
items.quote: With our product and capability breadth, combination of people in AI, and scale, we have a unique platform advantage that positions us to be the financial services provider of choice now and in the future, a position that is difficult for any competitor to match.

claims.text: The 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026) states that the firm is working on a referral model for workplace participants who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, which can begin as early as financial education and includes 401(k) plans and new 401(k) assets, to help them understand where they could use advice. Management said: "for those that might not yet have the advice-based relationship, we're working on that referral model. And that's something that can begin as early as the financial education spot, and it can also begin -- like I said, we have examples with 401(k)s and new 401(k) assets that come in that is not necessarily an IPO-specific workplace where we're really giving people that ability to better understand where they could use advice."

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the firm said Morgan Stanley at Work, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions Morgan Stanley as an early trusted advisor to more than 50,000 private companies, and that employees across its workplace companies benefit from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.

On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), the firm said its exclusive partnership with Carta means Carta will refer private companies with stock plans to Morgan Stanley as they move toward going public, and that the firm is committed to making that transition a seamless experience.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), the firm said the Carta relationship began as a referral-based model under which companies moving from the private side to the public side were referred to Morgan Stanley, and that it has seen conversions into its public-side business during the year.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the firm said clients are brought to E*TRADE through the corporate stock plan (workplace) context and, where appropriate, become fee-based flows to advisers: "we are very excited about the attachment points ultimately that bring clients to E*TRADE, that we are close with them in the corporate stock plan context, i.e., workplace, but then ultimately, where it's appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to the advisers."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), the firm said it uses LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform, to match workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitate engagement with financial advisors: "LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the firm said its investments go into referral models and products like LeadIQ to match individuals with advisers, with the goal of being their principal financial adviser: "They're going into creating our referral models. They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers. And our goal is to be their principal financial adviser."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the firm said it offers financial advice and financial wellness to clients, uses technology to match advisers to the right clients, and offers products, alternatives, and different types of solutions across different points in client life cycles.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the firm said it is using its scale to invest in broadening financial-advisor capabilities, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending: "We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said the firm has about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in its workplace pipeline and has invested to service these companies from early stages: "we have about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in terms of our workplace pipeline. So we've spent a lot of time thinking about how do we service some of these companies at the very early stages."

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management described the financial advisor, Workplace, and E*TRADE channels as each a category leader that together comprise the firm's strategic client acquisition model: "Our financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE, each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model."

On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), management said investments in self-directed and Workplace channels drive the firm's differentiated client acquisition funnel: "In Wealth Management, investments in our self-directed and Workplace channels drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management described the workplace channel as a powerful asset acquisition tool: "further evidence that our workplace channel serves as a powerful asset acquisition tool."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform and that the firm is well positioned to support these new relationships: "Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships."

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the firm reported that advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships accelerated to a record $99 billion for full-year 2025, compared with historical averages of around $60 billion per year: "Advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships accelerated, growing to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared to historical averages of around $60 billion per year."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), the firm reported that since 2020 it has generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE: "Since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), the firm said that, inclusive of Workplace assets on its platform prior to the acquisition of E*TRADE, the total value of adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion: "inclusive of Workplace assets on our platform prior to the acquisition of E*TRADE, the total value of adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), the firm said this represents roughly 20% of its current $5.8 trillion of adviser-led assets: "This represents roughly 20% of our current $5.8 trillion of adviser-led assets."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), the firm said it has previously cited about $60 billion of workplace migration per year and, three quarters into 2025, was exceeding those numbers on a full-year basis: "we've said that we've seen about $60 billion of migration per year. We're already three quarters into it, and we're exceeding those numbers from a full-year basis."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the firm said stock plan IPO flows represented just over half of overall net new assets in the quarter: "Stock plan IPO flows represented just over half of the overall NNA this quarter."

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states that through AdvisorChoice financial advisors can choose among six affiliation options: Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: The firm's AdvisorChoice spectrum spans Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services.
items.quote: EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) ADVISOR SELECT INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES

items.text: Raymond James states that financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

a1.RJF.reason: Passages explicitly list the firm's affiliation options under AdvisorChoice.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: For the Traditional Employee model, Raymond James states a payout of up to 50% plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: For the Advisor Select model, Raymond James states a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: For the Independent Contractor model, Raymond James states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits built through third-party partnerships.
items.quote: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: For the Corporate RIA model, Raymond James states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits built through third-party partnerships.
items.quote: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third-party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: For the Bank & Credit Union model, Raymond James states advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James during their transition.
items.quote: Get the support you need during your transition by receiving a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.

items.text: For the RIA & Custody Services model, Raymond James states advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package.
items.quote: Work with your RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation. Create your own benefits package.

items.text: Raymond James states that independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and therefore receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.
items.scope: Independent Contractor vs. employee affiliation options

items.text: Raymond James explains that independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their overhead costs, real estate and health insurance, and that the employee side has tiered payout systems where advisors move higher up the grid as production increases.
items.quote: the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance, et cetera, as you know, and so over the last year, in particular, much more of our recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side of the business.

a2.RJF.reason: Passages state payout percentages, benefit structures and cost responsibilities for each affiliation option.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states that growth in RCS client assets is partially due to transfers into RCS from its other financial advisor channels, and that it may continue to experience transfers to its RCS division.
items.quote: The growth in RCS client assets over time is partially due to transfers into RCS from our other financial advisor channels. We may continue to experience transfers to our RCS division; however, consistent with our experience in recent fiscal years, we would not expect these financial advisor transfers to significantly impact our results of operations.

items.text: Raymond James states that some prospective advisors do not know which affiliation option they want and that the firm works with them to evaluate the right affiliation option and its pros and cons.
items.quote: they're actually interested in understanding the various options and the various affiliation options, which those are the best conversations to have, which like we don't necessarily know exactly how we want to affiliate with Raymond James and how we want to run our business going forward.

a3.RJF.reason: Passages describe transfers into RCS from other channels and evaluation of affiliation options, but no fuller transition process is described.

a4.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Management describes AdvisorChoice as giving advisors the ability to match their professional goals to the right affiliation option, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Management says the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it has all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and that it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates as long as the advisor embraces the firm's culture, values and platform.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: Management says the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and that it is not a new venture.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them. It's not a new venture for us.

items.text: Management describes the model as combining multiple affiliation options, the best of both worlds, advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability to inspire and empower financial professionals.
items.quote: Multiple Affiliation Options Best of Both Worlds Advisor and Book Ownership RJF Stability Inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals.

items.text: Management says advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities because the firm offers an advisor- and client-focused culture together with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

a4.RJF.reason: Management quotes in multiple passages describe the affiliation-choice model.

a5.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Management lists the Private Client Group's strategic initiatives for the affiliation model as retention, advisor productivity and recruiting.
items.quote: RETENTION ADVISOR PRODUCTIVITY RECRUIT ING

items.text: Management states that growth starts with keeping existing advisors satisfied and having high retention of existing advisors.
items.quote: it starts with keeping our existing advisers satisfied and having high retention of our existing advisers.

items.text: Management states the firm does not lead with the highest check but wants competitive economics, leading with culture and capabilities and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics. Certainly, we have to have competitive economics, but we lead with culture and capabilities.

items.text: Management states the firm is focused on sustainable growth and quality over quantity and values independence to foster objective advice.
items.quote: We are focused on sustainable growth and quality over quantity.

items.text: The firm states its culture is rooted in putting clients first, acting with integrity, thinking long term, and valuing independence.
items.quote: we put clients first, • we act with integrity, • we think long term, and • we value independence.

a5.RJF.reason: Management states retention, recruiting, productivity, culture/capabilities, quality over quantity, long-term thinking and independence as priorities.

a6.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James says advisors are coming to it from wires, regionals and other independents, rather than from one firm.
items.quote: Advisors are coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents.

items.text: Raymond James describes private-equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel and aggressive competitive dynamic in advisor recruiting.
items.quote: The dynamic that's relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere.

items.text: Raymond James contrasts itself with competitors that compete with the largest check and change their compensation plans each year to cross-sell more bank products.
items.quote: many of our competitors compete with the largest check.

a6.RJF.reason: The firm names competitor categories (wires, regionals, other independents, PE-backed roll-ups) rather than specific firms.

a7.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James says a couple of OSJ relationships in its independent contractor division decided to leave the platform, with roughly $3 billion of AUA leaving in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2024.
items.quote: there are a couple of OSJ relationships in our independent contractor division who had decided to leave the platform. It takes time to effect these movements, but a portion of those assets left the firm in the fiscal fourth quarter, totaling roughly $3 billion of AUA.

items.text: Raymond James anticipated approximately $5 billion of assets associated with those departing OSJ firms would complete their transfers off the platform in early fiscal 2025.
items.quote: We anticipate approximately $5 billion of assets associated with these firms to complete their transfers off the platform in early fiscal 2025.

items.text: Raymond James says the departure of primarily one large branch in its Independent Contractor Division impacted net new assets by approximately $5 billion of AUA.
items.quote: the departure of primarily one large branch in our Independent Contractor Division. The impact was approximately $5 billion of AUA.

items.text: Raymond James says it has historically had about 1% regretted attrition, and that the biggest movement of people to the RIA channel has gone to its own RIA so the firm kept the assets.
items.quote: We've historically had that 1% type of regretted attrition, but we don't see anything big on the leaving side. The biggest movement of people that have gone to RIA, fortunately, have gone to our RIA, so we've kept the assets.

items.text: Raymond James says it expects to lose a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets through bank M&A.
items.quote: From time to time with bank M&A, next quarter, for example, there'll be a platform that we'll lose just through bank M&A. I think it's a $2.7 billion of assets.

a7.RJF.reason: Passages describe departures from the independent contractor channel and a bank-M&A platform loss.

a8.RJF.label: fact

items.quote: we had approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

items.quote: we had approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it has all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and that it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates as long as the advisor embraces the firm's culture, values and platform: “we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we’re agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), management said the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and that it is not a new venture: “we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them. It’s not a new venture for us.”

Raymond James Financial: In the investor day deck published June 5, 2025, management describes the model as combining multiple affiliation options, the best of both worlds, advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities because the firm offers an advisor- and client-focused culture together with leading technology, products and solutions: “advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.”

Raymond James Financial: In the investor day deck published June 5, 2025, management lists the Private Client Group's strategic initiatives for the affiliation model as retention, advisor productivity and recruiting: “RETENTION ADVISOR PRODUCTIVITY RECRUIT ING”.

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management stated that growth starts with keeping existing advisors satisfied and having high retention of existing advisors: “it starts with keeping our existing advisers satisfied and having high retention of our existing advisers.”

Raymond James Financial: In its 2025 Form 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025), the firm states its culture is rooted in putting clients first, acting with integrity, thinking long term, and valuing independence: “we put clients first, • we act with integrity, • we think long term, and • we value independence.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), Raymond James said advisors are coming to it from wires, regionals and other independents, rather than from one firm: “Advisors are coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), Raymond James described private-equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel and aggressive competitive dynamic in advisor recruiting: “The dynamic that’s relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), Raymond James contrasted itself with competitors that compete with the largest check and change their compensation plans each year to cross-sell more bank products, saying: “many of our competitors compete with the largest check.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), Raymond James said the departure of primarily one large branch in its Independent Contractor Division impacted net new assets by approximately $5 billion of assets under administration: “the departure of primarily one large branch in our Independent Contractor Division. The impact was approximately $5 billion of AUA.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), Raymond James said it has historically had about 1% regretted attrition, and that the biggest movement of people to the RIA channel has gone to its own RIA so the firm kept the assets: “We’ve historically had that 1% type of regretted attrition, but we don’t see anything big on the leaving side. The biggest movement of people that have gone to RIA, fortunately, have gone to our RIA, so we’ve kept the assets.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), Raymond James said it expects to lose a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets through bank M&A: “From time to time with bank M&A, next quarter, for example, there’ll be a platform that we’ll lose just through bank M&A. Merrill: Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) foundational beliefs, as stated in the November 2025 investor day deck, include that growth of fully advised client relationships drives financial outcomes and that having the best advisors enables exceptional client outcomes.
Merrill: On the second-quarter 2026 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Bank of America's CFO said GWIM continued to demonstrate the strength of its advice-led, relationship-based model.

The comparison is valid on this evidence as a qualitative comparison of earnings models, but it is not a same-basis numeric comparison because the firms use different revenue definitions, units, periods, and scopes. The driver of the difference is that Schwab's direct-to-investor brokerage and bank earns predominantly through the cash-spread (net interest) model on client cash, while the advisor-led models earn predominantly through asset-based fees on client assets. Schwab's 2025 10-K reports net interest revenue of $11.8 billion within $23.9 billion of total net revenues in 2025 and states client cash is a significant funding source; trade-press reporting attributes Schwab's model to the cash-spread business model, reports net interest revenues were 49.3% of Schwab's 2025 revenues, and reports only 5% of Schwab retail households are in fee-based advice. In contrast, the advisor-led firms describe asset-based fees as the core of their earnings on client assets: Morgan Stanley's 10-K states asset management revenues are generally based on the net asset value of the account; Edward Jones' 10-K states fee revenue is composed of asset-based fees based on the average daily market value of client assets plus account and activity fees; Raymond James' 10-K states the Private Client Group generally charges asset-based fees or sales commissions; and Bank of America's CFO stated GWIM is primarily a fee-based advice-driven model with about 30% of revenue as net interest income. Morgan Stanley also states that any revenues earned by Wealth Management on client assets will vary depending upon the services and products provided.

items.text: Capgemini states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, with future success defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations rather than just their assets.
items.quote: The wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice: future success will be defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations, rather than just their assets.

items.text: Capgemini describes the Later horizon of its roadmap as reaching full operating-model maturity: autonomous portfolio delivery, AI-enabled estate and tax planning embedded in client journeys, and a firm-wide intelligence system that institutionalizes relationship knowledge across RM transitions and client generations.
items.quote: In the Later horizon, the operating model reaches full maturity: autonomous portfolio delivery, AI-enabled estate and tax planning embedded in client journeys, and a firm-wide intelligence system that institutionalizes relationship knowledge across RM transitions and client generations.

items.text: Deloitte says clients want advice that is always on and frictionless, while advisers currently spend nearly 70% of their time on behind-the-scenes work and only 30% building client relationships.
items.quote: Clients want advice that’s always on and frictionless, while advisers are busy managing larger, more complex books. Advisers spend nearly 70% of their time on behind-the-scenes work, leaving just 30% for where they add the most value—building client relationships.

items.text: Deloitte says AI is no longer just a productivity tool but a source of competitive differentiation, with winners using it to create a simpler adviser experience and unlock hyper-personalization at scale.
items.quote: AI is no longer just a productivity tool—it can be a source of competitive differentiation. Those that succeed may be the firms that use it to create a fundamentally simpler adviser experience, unlock hyper-personalization at scale, and help their advisers grow faster than anyone else in the industry.

items.text: Schwab identifies key trends reinforcing its confidence, including growing demand for holistic advice, desire for ease across wealth, banking and investing, rising investor expectations for sophisticated personalized solutions, and accelerating wealth tech innovation.
items.quote:
Growing demand for holistic advice

Desire for ease across wealth, banking, & investing Rising investor expectations for sophisticated, personalized solutions Accelerating wealth tech innovation RIAs seeking to differentiate & scale

items.text: Accenture reports 97% of surveyed wealth executives say AI will have a transformative effect on the future of financial advice to a moderate or great extent in the next three years.
items.quote: say AI will have a transformative effect on the future of financial advice to a moderate or great extent in the next three years

items.text: Edward Jones states it is pursuing initiatives to meet clients' planning, investing, saving, spending, borrowing and comprehensive needs, including Financial Planning Services, High Net Worth, Workplace, and a new digital platform targeting Next Generation investors.
items.quote: These initiatives include both potential future solutions currently in development as well as recently launched products and solutions such as Financial Planning Services, where clients receive a more personalized experience with additional planning capabilities.

a1.all.reason: Passages state the overall future state of how clients will receive financial advice.

a2.all.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says clients will engage in person, on the phone, on the web, on mobile, or via AI at different times and for different activities.
items.quote: At different times in their lives and for different activities, clients engage with us in person, on the phone, web, mobile, or via AI.

items.text: Schwab says its multichannel service model delivers 24/7 support via online, mobile, telephone and branch channels.
items.quote: Our multichannel service model delivers award-winning, 24/7 support via online, mobile, telephone, and branch channels, ensuring clients receive consistent service regardless of asset level or preferred method of engagement.

items.text: Wealthtender reports one-third of surveyed participants say an advisor's physical location does not matter because they prefer to meet exclusively online.
items.quote: One-third of survey participants said an advisor’s physical location doesn’t matter because they prefer to meet exclusively online.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says its Wealth Management business competes across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels.
items.quote: advisor led, workplace and digital direct

items.text: Capgemini says clients can interact directly with specialists via digital channels or work through their lead RM, who coordinates specialist engagement.
items.quote: Clients can interact directly with specialists via digital channels or work through their lead RM, who coordinates specialist engagement and dynamically routes standardized requests to other RMs or service teams.

items.text: Schwab says total client interactions within its branches, on chat, email and phones are up 19% year-over-year.
items.quote: Total client interactions within our branches on chat, email, and on the phones are up 19% year-over-year

a2.all.reason: Passages state the channels through which clients will receive financial advice.

a3.all.label: fact

items.text: Schwab introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant providing U.S. retail clients conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights.
items.quote: Introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab’s tools and insights

items.text: Schwab partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs it serves.
items.quote: Partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs Schwab serves

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes early AI use cases including the DevGen AI tool, Parable, and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform matching workplace and self-directed relationships with financial advisors.
items.quote: These include the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, and LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Raymond James lists AI tools in its pipeline, including RJnet and Advisor Access GenAI Search, Zoom AI Meeting Summaries, GenAI Search, Microsoft CoPilot and the NASH Platform.
items.quote:
RJnet & Advisor Access GenAI Search

Zoom AI Meeting Summaries

Advisor Access Recommended Apps

GenAI Search

Microsoft CoPilot

NASH Platform

items.text: Deloitte says Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups and logs notes into the CRM, and that Altruist's Hazel AI can analyze tax returns and portfolio data to generate tax-planning insights.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley’s AI Debrief, for example, automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the customer relationship management system

items.text: Deloitte says emerging platforms such as Altruist's Hazel AI can analyze tax returns and portfolio data to generate tax-planning insights and scenarios in seconds.
items.quote: Emerging platforms such as Altruist’s Hazel AI—which can analyze tax returns and portfolio data to generate tax-planning insights and scenarios in seconds

items.text: Bank of America says it has over 300 AI use cases approved, of which 114 are live generative AI use cases.
items.quote: we had over 300 AI use cases approved, all of which have good economics, of which 114 are live generative AI use cases.

items.text: Schwab says it will introduce the first of several AI assistants enabling clients to interact via chat and voice, with actions such as setting beneficiaries.
items.quote: Starting over the summer, we will introduce the first of several AI assistants that will enable our clients to interact with chat and voice to address their most frequent service and support needs.

items.text: Edward Jones is partnering with Aboon, an AI-driven third-party administrator, to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool for advisors.
items.quote: Edward Jones has partnered with Aboon, an AI-driven third-party administrator, and Retirement Plan Advisory Group (part of Great Gray Group) to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool.

a3.all.reason: Passages state the technology and tools that will be used to deliver financial advice.

a4.all.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says 77% of U.S. investors use AI today, while more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside AI technology.
items.quote: 77% of U.S. investors use AI today. And at the same time, more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside AI technology.

items.text: McKinsey says the AI replacement thesis is mostly false for core advice segments, where nearly 80% of affluent households still prefer a human relationship, though an AI takeover might be possible for standardized lower-touch models and younger clients.
items.quote: the replacement thesis is mostly false for core advice segments, where nearly 80 percent of affluent households still prefer a human relationship, though an AI takeover might indeed be possible for standardized, lower-touch service models and for younger clients

items.text: Adobe's Jose Thomas says there will always be a need for human advisors because life goals, trade-offs and emotions cannot be automated; technology will handle research and complexity while advisors focus on judgment and empathy.
items.quote: There will always be a need for human advisors in wealth management because life goals, trade-offs, and emotions can't be automated. What will change is their effectiveness. Technology will handle research and complexity, while advisors focus on judgment, empathy, and guiding clients through decisions that matter most.

items.text: Deloitte says agentic AI brings in the human adviser when judgment or a client conversation is needed.
items.quote: while bringing in the human adviser when judgment or a client conversation is needed.

items.text: Raymond James says AI will not replace advisers; advisers who use AI will replace advisers who do not use AI.
items.quote: AI will not replace advisers. Advisers who use AI will replace advisers who do not use AI.

items.text: Capgemini says firms should maintain a human-in-the-loop environment in which AI rebalances portfolios while relationship managers own critical decisions.
items.quote: Maintain a human-in-the-loop environment in which AI rebalances portfolios while relationship managers own critical decisions, and their successful client rapport influences their rewards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is evolving from pure efficiency to effectiveness with co-piloting and super agents that use historical context between financial adviser and client.
items.quote: where she is well aware of the past interactions and how that might drive against certain market dynamics, future action. And so that co-piloting, I think, is something that Jed Finn under the leadership of Andy Saperstein is spending a lot of time on

items.text: Capgemini describes an Adaptive Experience AI Engine that dynamically tailors content depth, tone and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context.
items.quote: An Adaptive Experience AI Engine with Knowledge Management as a Service (KMaaS) dynamically tailors content depth, tone, and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context.

items.text: Capgemini describes a Unified Client Semantics Profile that consolidates behavioral, goal and portfolio intelligence into a persistent knowledge layer so context flows across digital and advisor interactions.
items.quote: A Unified Client Semantics Profile consolidates behavioral, goal, and portfolio intelligence into a persistent knowledge layer, ensuring context flows seamlessly across digital and advisor interactions.

items.text: Deloitte says faster responses, more tailored insights and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards for clients.
items.quote: Faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards.

items.text: Pictet COO Laurent Gaillard, in Capgemini, says consistent, contextually relevant advice will be delivered across every client and every interaction regardless of who the RM is.
items.quote: consistent, contextually relevant advice will be delivered across every client and every interaction, regardless of who the RM is.

items.text: Schwab says AI is accelerating its strategy by personalizing client experiences, enhancing productivity and driving scalable growth.
items.quote: personalizing client experiences, enhancing productivity, and driving scalable growth.

items.text: Capgemini describes a reimagined AI-powered desktop that delivers a humanlike, empathetic, personalized and contextual experience.
items.quote: a reimagined, AI-powered desktop that delivers a humanlike, empathetic, personalized, and contextual experience through three integrated capabilities.

items.quote: coordinating specialists in tax, estate planning, lending, philanthropy, and non-financial value-added services.

items.text: Capgemini says advice will be shaped by client context rather than institutional templates, coordinated across tax, estate, lending, health and life planning.
items.quote: advice will be shaped by client context rather than institutional templates - coordinated across tax, estate, lending, health, and life planning.

items.text: Schwab says clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust and estate services, tax-aware strategies, banking and lending.
items.quote: clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, tax-aware strategies, and more. With our bank, retail investors can manage their day-to-day financial lives with checking, savings, and bill pay while also turning to us for lending needs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is investing in broadening capabilities for financial advisors including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Goldman Sachs Asset Management says retirement strategies should personalize and humanize the retirement experience, an evolution in plan design, participant support and advice.
items.quote: This underscores the need to personalize and humanize the retirement experience-an essential evolution in plan design, participant support, and advice.

items.text: Capgemini says Standard Chartered Bank's partnerships with Bupa Global and WHOOP show how wealth firms are embedding health and wellness into client offerings.
items.quote: Standard Chartered Bank's November 2025 partnerships with premium international health insurer Bupa Global and Boston-based wearable technology company WHOOP demonstrate how wealth firms are embedding health and wellness into client offerings

claims.text: Schwab: Schwab's press release (published October 15, 2026) states it introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant providing U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights. Why it might matter: Schwab was recognized as one of Fortune's 2026 Most Innovative Companies.

Schwab: Schwab's press release (published October 15, 2026) states it partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs it serves. Why it might matter: Morgan Stanley also describes early AI use cases, including the DevGen AI tool, Parable, and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform matching workplace and self-directed relationships with financial advisors.

Raymond James: Raymond James's investor day deck (published June 5, 2025) lists AI tools in its pipeline, including RJnet and Advisor Access GenAI Search, Zoom AI Meeting Summaries, Advisor Access Recommended Apps, GenAI Search, Microsoft CoPilot, and the NASH Platform. Why it might matter: Schwab has likewise introduced Charley, an AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients conversational access to its tools and insights.

Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Schwab management said 77% of U.S. investors use AI today, while more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside AI technology. Why it might matter: Schwab says that combination of people and technology has always been central to Schwab and is a key source of its differentiation.

Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Schwab management said it is ready to provide access when clients want it and will move to 24/7 trading if clients want it. Why it might matter: Schwab says it has plenty of overseas clients and people working during the day who value participating outside regular market hours.

Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Schwab management said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials, while roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high-net-worth and high-net-worth households. Why it might matter: Schwab says it is well positioned to continue serving future generations when that wealth is passed on.

Edward Jones: Trade press (published September 30, 2026) reports that Edward Jones has partnered with Aboon, an AI-driven third-party administrator, and Retirement Plan Advisory Group (part of Great Gray Group) to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool. Why it might matter: Edward Jones hopes the new technology will help its advisors better serve business owners and their employees.

Raymond James: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Raymond James management said AI will not replace advisers; advisers who use AI will replace advisers who do not use AI. Why it might matter: Raymond James says freeing advisers from middle-office work lets them spend more time developing personal relationships with clients and prospects, which is going to win the day.

Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Schwab management said clients will engage in person, on the phone, on the web, on mobile, or via AI at different times in their lives and for different activities. Why it might matter: Schwab says clients value that flexibility, and that in every interaction across every channel it combines the best of people and the power of AI.

Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Schwab management said AI is accelerating its strategy by personalizing client experiences, enhancing productivity, and driving scalable growth. Why it might matter: Schwab says its greatest advantage comes from combining people with AI-powered capabilities to create deeper relationships that scale with clients' needs.

Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Schwab management said clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, tax-aware strategies, banking, and lending. Why it might matter: Schwab says the RIAs it serves value its bank because they don't have to introduce another relationship to their clients.

Bank of America: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Bank of America management said it has over 300 AI use cases approved, of which 114 are live generative AI use cases. Why it might matter: Bank of America says these tools are designed to help its customer relationship managers prepare more thoroughly for client meetings.

Bank of America: Bank of America Private Bank (published June 17, 2026) says younger investors allocate nearly half as much to stocks as older generations, while allocating more to alternatives (15%) and crypto (13%) than older investors. Why it might matter: Bank of America Private Bank says 67% of younger investors believe traditional stocks and bonds can no longer deliver above-average returns.

J.P. Morgan: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (published June 12, 2026) says all data is aggregated, completely anonymized, and kept confidential and secure, and that all unique identifiable information, including names, account numbers, addresses, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers, is removed before researchers receive it. Why it might matter: J.P. Morgan Asset Management says it has security protocols designed to ensure all customer data is kept confidential and secure, using reasonable physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards designed to comply with federal standards.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, with future success defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations rather than just their assets. Why it might matter: Capgemini adds that this approach focuses on delivering unique experiences and networking opportunities that extend beyond traditional financial returns.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) describes the Later horizon of its roadmap as reaching full operating-model maturity: autonomous portfolio delivery, AI-enabled estate and tax planning embedded in client journeys, and a firm-wide intelligence system that institutionalizes relationship knowledge across RM transitions and client generations. Why it might matter: Capgemini also describes a Unified Client Semantics Profile that consolidates behavioral, goal, and portfolio intelligence into a persistent knowledge layer so context flows across digital and advisor interactions.
claims.source_label: Research research 2026-06-03, p.9 [research]; Research research 2026-06-03, p.36 [research]

claims.text: Schwab: Schwab's investor day deck (published May 14, 2026) identifies key trends: growing demand for holistic advice, desire for ease across wealth, banking, and investing, rising investor expectations for sophisticated, personalized solutions, accelerating wealth tech innovation, and RIAs seeking to differentiate and scale. Why it might matter: Capgemini separately states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice.
claims.source_label: SCHW deck 2026-05-14, p.120 [IR]; Research research 2026-06-03, p.9 [research]

claims.text: Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) says clients can interact directly with specialists via digital channels or work through their lead RM, who coordinates specialist engagement and dynamically routes standardized requests to other RMs or service teams. Why it might matter: Capgemini says this accommodates different preferences for autonomy versus guided support.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) quotes Adobe's Jose Thomas saying there will always be a need for human advisors in wealth management because life goals, trade-offs, and emotions can't be automated; technology will handle research and complexity while advisors focus on judgment, empathy, and guiding clients through decisions that matter most. Why it might matter: Capgemini adds that core advisory activities—understanding client goals, navigating family dynamics, guiding clients through uncertainty, and coordinating across complex needs—cannot be automated.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) says firms should maintain a human-in-the-loop environment in which AI rebalances portfolios while relationship managers own critical decisions. Why it might matter: Capgemini says relationship managers' successful client rapport influences their rewards.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) describes an Adaptive Experience AI Engine with Knowledge Management as a Service that dynamically tailors content depth, tone, and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context. Why it might matter: Capgemini says this enables client journeys to evolve in real time rather than relying on static segmentation.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) describes a Unified Client Semantics Profile that consolidates behavioral, goal, and portfolio intelligence into a persistent knowledge layer, ensuring context flows seamlessly across digital and advisor interactions. Why it might matter: Capgemini says this persistent knowledge layer supports explainable recommendations while equipping relationship managers with governed AI copilots, personalized nudges, and meeting intelligence.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) describes a reimagined AI-powered desktop that delivers a humanlike, empathetic, personalized, and contextual experience through three integrated capabilities. Why it might matter: Capgemini says this work focused on fast-tracking experience modernization while maintaining trust and human oversight.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) says Standard Chartered Bank's November 2025 partnerships with premium international health insurer Bupa Global and wearable technology company WHOOP demonstrate how wealth firms are embedding health and wellness into client offerings. Why it might matter: Capgemini says this integrates insurance and wearable tracking into a coordinated service model for Standard Chartered's wealth management clients across key markets.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) says the intelligence layer will synthesize fragmented client data—behavioral patterns, contextual signals, and relationship history—into a coherent and actionable view, surfacing insights that align client needs with firm capabilities at the moments that matter. Why it might matter: Capgemini says life transitions, liquidity events, and behavioral signals will increasingly determine when and how firms interact with clients, replacing calendar-driven review cycles with relevance-driven ones.

Capgemini: Capgemini (published June 3, 2026) says AI predicts triggers and opportunities, enabling RMs to engage clients at moments of real relevance rather than in response to periodic reviews or client-initiated interactions. Why it might matter: Capgemini says firms should embed guardrails and compliance parameters so relationship managers can act confidently on AI-generated recommendations within defined boundaries.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says clients want advice that is always on and frictionless, while advisers currently spend nearly 70% of their time on behind-the-scenes work and only 30% building client relationships. Why it might matter: Deloitte adds that artificial intelligence, especially agentic execution, has the potential to flip that equation.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says AI is no longer just a productivity tool but a source of competitive differentiation, with winners using it to create a simpler adviser experience, unlock hyper-personalization at scale, and help their advisers grow faster than anyone else in the industry. Why it might matter: Deloitte frames this against a US$124 trillion generational wealth transfer and a widening adviser shortage, saying wealth management stands at an inflection point.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the customer relationship management system, and that Altruist's Hazel AI can analyze tax returns and portfolio data to generate tax-planning insights. Why it might matter: Deloitte says this reduces manual documentation and frees advisers to spend more time on client conversations rather than administrative tasks.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says emerging platforms such as Altruist's Hazel AI can analyze tax returns and portfolio data to generate tax-planning insights and scenarios in seconds. Why it might matter: Deloitte says this illustrates how AI can handle complex analytical tasks that previously required hours of manual work.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says agentic AI brings in the human adviser when judgment or a client conversation is needed. Why it might matter: Deloitte says this allows firms to serve less complex clients more economically while still delivering personalized advice.

Deloitte: Deloitte (published May 20, 2026) says faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards for clients. Why it might matter: Deloitte says this shift presents a real opportunity to address one of wealth management's most persistent challenges: client experience.

UBS: UBS (published April 22, 2026) says most next-generation respondents favor a blended approach to communicating (83%), combining digital convenience with in-person interaction. Why it might matter: UBS reports that, as one inheritor put it, to make a difference, wealth experts need to get personal.

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley management said it is evolving from pure efficiency to effectiveness with co-piloting and super agents that use historical context between the financial adviser and client. Why it might matter: Morgan Stanley describes the effectiveness dimension—using historical context between the financial adviser and client—as super compelling.

McKinsey: McKinsey (published April 8, 2026) says the replacement thesis is mostly false for core advice segments, where nearly 80 percent of affluent households still prefer a human relationship, though an AI takeover might be possible for standardized, lower-touch service models and for younger clients. Why it might matter: McKinsey notes that its research shows interest in holistic advice rose from 29 percent in 2018 to 52 percent in 2023.

McKinsey: McKinsey (published April 8, 2026) says fee pressure will be uneven, manifesting as demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points. Why it might matter: McKinsey notes that fee rates for relationships of more than $1 million have remained remarkably steady since 2019 even as digital tools have proliferated.

Bank of America: Bank of America's investor day deck (published November 5, 2025) describes a wealth continuum in which mass market clients get a predominantly digital experience, mass affluent get guidance delivered at scale, high net worth get dedicated advice and customizable solutions for complex needs, and ultra high net worth get a sophisticated approach to managing generational wealth. Why it might matter: McKinsey separately says nearly 80 percent of affluent households still prefer a human relationship in core advice segments.
claims.source_label: BAC deck 2025-11-05, p.6 [IR]; Research research 2026-04-08, p.3 [research]

claims.text: Cerulli: Cerulli (published March 25, 2026) says the mass-affluent segment is a $25 trillion market comprising 46.9 million households that seeks involved advisor relationships, which will benefit providers that can best offer streamlined advisory services at scale. Why it might matter: Cerulli notes this segment is typically younger and less advised.

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states it is pursuing initiatives to meet clients' planning, investing, saving, spending, borrowing, and comprehensive needs, including Financial Planning Services, High Net Worth, Workplace, and a new digital platform targeting Next Generation investors. Why it might matter: Bank of America similarly describes a wealth continuum in which clients receive increasingly dedicated advice as their wealth and complexity grow.

Schwab: Schwab's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states its multichannel service model delivers 24/7 support via online, mobile, telephone, and branch channels, ensuring clients receive consistent service regardless of asset level or preferred method of engagement. Why it might matter: Schwab says it offers several relationship models designed to meet differing levels of financial complexity, engagement, and service preference.

Schwab: Schwab's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states Schwab Private Client Services serves clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets and Schwab Private Wealth Services serves clients with more than $10 million, with enhanced, relationship-based experiences. Why it might matter: Schwab says these enhanced experiences include dedicated service teams, specialized expertise, expedited processing, pricing advantages, and access to exclusive product offerings.

Bank of America: Bank of America's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states it and its regulators have an increased focus on privacy, information security, and emerging technologies such as AI, including the collection, use, and sharing of data and safeguarding of personally identifiable information and corporate data. Why it might matter: Bank of America says these matters have resulted in, and will likely continue to result in, related litigation, including class actions, or government action.

Schwab: Schwab's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) defines privacy risk as the risk of unauthorized collection, use, storage, or sharing of personal information, including data incidents and other mismanagement of personal information. Why it might matter: Schwab says it manages privacy risk through policies, procedures, and controls reasonably designed to achieve or monitor compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states its Wealth Management business competes across advisor-led, workplace, and digital direct channels. Why it might matter: Morgan Stanley says its ability to compete across these channels is affected by factors including its brand and reputation, the breadth, depth, and pricing of its product offerings, and its technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.

Cerulli: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) estimates Millennials will inherit $46 trillion over the next 25 years, while Gen X stands to inherit $14 trillion in the next 10 years. Why it might matter: Cerulli notes Gen X stands to inherit the greatest portion of assets in the next 10 years, totaling $14 trillion to Millennials' $8 trillion over that period.

Schwab: On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), Schwab management said total client interactions within its branches, on chat, email, and phones are up 19% year-over-year. Why it might matter: Schwab adds that clients are highly engaged with both Schwab and the markets, and that it exceeded 500 million digital client logins across mobile and web for the third consecutive quarter.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), Morgan Stanley management described early AI use cases including the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform matching workplace and self-directed relationships with financial advisors. Why it might matter: Morgan Stanley says these early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, are showing progress.

Wealthtender: Wealthtender (published August 13, 2025) reports that one-third of surveyed participants say an advisor's physical location does not matter because they prefer to meet exclusively online. Why it might matter: Wealthtender says this represents a fundamental change in how financial relationships can work.

Wealthtender: Wealthtender (published August 13, 2025) says common fee models include asset-based fees (typically 0.5% to 1.5% annually), hourly rates ($150-$500+ per hour), flat project fees, or monthly subscription fees. Why it might matter: Wealthtender notes that financial advisor fees vary significantly based on services provided, asset level, and the advisor's fee structure.

Accenture: Accenture (published June 23, 2025) reports that 97% of surveyed wealth executives say AI will have a transformative effect on the future of financial advice to a moderate or great extent in the next three years. Why it might matter: Accenture also reports that 47% of surveyed executives believe AI will have a direct, measurable, and consistent impact on the client-adviser relationship in the next 12 months.

CFPB: CFPB (published June 6, 2025) says the internet offers unprecedented accessibility, available anytime and anywhere. Why it might matter: CFPB says the internet creates spaces where consumers can seek information without fear of judgment and verify what they learn.

Cerulli: Cerulli (published May 28, 2025) says fee-based payments are preferred by 36% of affluent investors. Why it might matter: Cerulli attributes this to fee-based advisors' compensation being tied to portfolio performance rather than to selling particular products.

McKinsey: McKinsey (published February 10, 2025) says, according to PriceMetrix by McKinsey, that fee rates for $1.0 million to $1.5 million advisory relationships have stayed at an average since 2019. Why it might matter: McKinsey says that after a period of fee compression from 2013 to 2018, advisory fee rates have stabilized.
